hypothesis: Built as 64-lane waves on a gfx1102 (RDNA3), the decode's FP4 expert group runs 37-39 % faster than as 32-lane waves (a microbenchmark: 0.64 -> 0.39 ms per expert), and the HIP tier's decode spends much of its time there, so decode gets faster with the same greedy text.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture, REAP-pruned to 132 experts x 43 layers (79 GB), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -j16 deepseek-v4 HIP=1 HIP_ARCH=gfx1102 ROCM_HOME=/usr HIP_WAVE64=<0|1> (one binary per arm, same commit); deepseek_v4 <model> 'Count from 1 to 300, separated by single spaces.' --max-tokens 200 with the environment in config (--vram 5 as CUDA_EXPERT_GB=5); the arms alternate (trial, baseline) three times; tok_s = (generated - 1) / after_first from the engine's `timing` line (decode throughput)

hardware.ram: 62 GB DDR5 (auto memory budget, about 57 GiB available)
hardware.storage: Apacer AS2280Q4U 4TB NVMe (PCIe 4.0 x4), ext4, direct aligned reads
hardware.os: Gentoo Linux 7.3.5, gcc 16.2.1, ROCm/HIP 7.16.0 (clang 23.1.5), AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT 8 GB (gfx1102, PCIe 4.0 x8; also the display GPU, desktop running)

config.args: 'Count from 1 to 300, separated by single spaces.' --max-tokens 200
